profile.regional_context: QTS was founded in 2003 by Chad Williams, went public via IPO in 2013, and was acquired by Blackstone (via Blackstone Infrastructure Partners and BREIT) for approximately $10 billion, completed August 31, 2021. QTS is headquartered in Overland Park, Kansas.
profile.facility_type_note: Part of QTS's Northern Virginia campus, spanning Loudoun County (Ashburn-Shellhorn, Ashburn-Moran, Ashburn Lockridge buildings), Prince William County (Manassas DC1, DC2, DC5), and Sterling (Ashburn 1, Ashburn 2). Northern Virginia is confirmed by Wikipedia as one of QTS's primary operating regions, alongside the separate Richmond, VA campus recorded elsewhere in this registry.

reading.body:
QTS Manassas DC1 is part of a planned 6-building, 105-acre campus in Prince William County with a stated capacity of 190+ MW of critical campus power. This is the published total across all six buildings, not the capacity of DC1 alone; the operator has not disclosed how that total is distributed among individual facilities. At typical AI training densities of 40 kW per rack, 190 MW of IT load would support roughly 4,750 racks, though this figure assumes the full campus capacity is dedicated to compute and excludes the overhead of cooling, infrastructure, and redundancy.

The campus sits within QTS's broader Northern Virginia footprint, which spans Loudoun County and Prince William County with at least seven named facilities. Virginia has 23 facilities with published megawatt figures in this registry, totaling 1,375.4 MW. This campus ranks 24th in published capacity for the state, meaning it does not individually break into the top tier of disclosed Virginia data center capacity, though it represents part of QTS's regional concentration.

QTS acquired Blackstone ownership in August 2021 and operates this facility as hyperscale infrastructure. The operator's own specification page is the source for the 190+ MW figure and campus details. No certifications, utility interconnect details, or power supply redundancy are published in available operator materials.
